PACKET-10 - blind image reading (unverified)

Exposure statement: No identification of the work or author was revealed to me before or during this reading. I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files in this packet (and listed the directory); I did not read packet.json. Visible on the leaf itself are modern pencil notes: "Stams, STA, Frag. 78r" / "78v" and, on the recto, an older pencil note "Vd/M,9 (1548)" (a shelf/binding reference, not an identification of the text). I have not identified the text and have not used any edition.
Process note: the recto overview (image-001) came back trimmed from my context ("[media removed: request limit]"), so the 78r layout description rests on the native tiles image-002..007, which I did see.

== LAYOUT SURVEY ==

Images: image-001 = reduced overview, face "78r"; image-002..007 = native tiles of that face. image-008 = reduced overview, face "78v"; image-009..014 = native tiles of that face.

Observations:
- Irregularly cut parchment fragment (lower part narrower, corners clipped), upright. Probably reused in a binding: fold lines, a turned-in strip at the left of 78r / right of 78v, holes, stains.
- Two script sizes, clearly hierarchical: a large gothic textualis for a main text (short column(s) in the middle of the page, c. 20 lines visible) and a much smaller gothic hand for a surrounding text block that frames the main text above, at the outer side, and below. Tentative interpretation: main text with a frame gloss/commentary.
- In the small-script block, lemmata are underlined (in ink) and introduced by red paragraph marks (red C-shaped pilcrows); allegation-style references (abbreviations like "ff.", "C.", "di.", "q.", "l.", "§", "ar(gumentum)") are frequent.
- Main text: red enlarged initial S (2 lines) on 78r; red-touched initial letters and red paragraph marks within the main column on both faces.
- 78r: on the left there is a separate strip (a turned-in / pasted piece, separated by a seam) carrying parts of two narrower columns in the same large main-text script, plus a few lines of small gloss script above them. On 78v the corresponding turned-in strip is at the upper right.
- 78v: two main-text columns visible (left one damaged in the middle), gloss above, at left, and below. In the damaged middle of the left main column, and below it, there is reversed (mirror-image) printed text and Roman numerals (e.g. reversed "CLXXII", "...EQVN...", "sacramentali"), apparently offset or adhering paper from a printed book; this is not part of the manuscript text.
- No running title visible (top margin cut away).

Selected spans: the complete main-text column of 78r; the main-text strip at left of 78r (line ends/beginnings only); the gloss right of the 78r main text (lemma sequence); the lower gloss on 78r (partial); on 78v both main-text columns as far as legible, the gloss lemmata at upper left/top, and the lower gloss block. Not fully read: much of the gloss on both faces (small script, abbreviated, stained) - I give sample lines only; the far-left strip of 78r below its top lines; the right-hand narrow gloss strip on 78v below.

Conventions: (abc) = proposed expansion; word? = uncertain; [illegible] = not readable by me; [cut] = text runs off the fragment. Line numbers counted from the top of each tile.
